rows.what the ink shows: After Supposons, the short upper flick and low connected remnants are covered by two long cancellation strokes; a downward loop toward the end survives, but the interior letter bodies and word break do not securely establish maintenant que.

After the surviving phi-f stem, a low initial curve, crossed middle traces, small upper points and a terminal upright/exit remain beneath several dense cancellation strokes. They suggest existe, but the middle letter sequence is not independently recoverable from this ink.

The superscript at the upper right of Delta is a filled oblique wedge rising to the right, with no clean thin horizontal bar. It occupies the expected superscript position, but the broad overdrawn shape does not securely determine a minus sign.

The final cancelled sign after Delta existe has a long downstroke below the lower strike and a hooked upper-right loop joining the upper strike. Separate s and dotted-i forms are not recoverable; the candidate si remains uncertain.

The Greek sign has an open upper bowl with separate left and right arms and a central upright descending through it; the small f lies below and right with its own cross stroke. There is no closed oval joining the arms.

The cancelled word preserves a rounded initial e, crossing strokes of x, an upper i point, compact s, a tall t with cross stroke and a low final exit; the zigzag cancellation passes through the bodies but leaves the sequence legible.

Immediately before the tall f, a short low curved s trace survives under the horizontal strike, followed by the distinctly separated i point above the line. The two-letter group is separated from the f.

At the beginning of the deleted line, a small e-like opening and following loop remain, but the connecting bodies run into the cancellation line and the inserted writing above; the second word is reduced to horizontal remnants. The full étant son cannot be distinguished securely.

Below the deleted prose, the phi has a small loop and long descending stem. Its lower-right index clearly contains a separate straight 1, a plus with crossing arms, and a long f stem with a crossbar, despite the zigzag above them.
After the deleted indexed phi, a curved e opening is followed by the tall t upright and crossbar; the t exit continues right beneath the deletion stroke.

In the formula index before +f, the right stem extends above a left diagonal branch that meets it partway down, forming lambda. This differs visibly from the isolated straight 1 in the cancelled phi index directly above.

A separate flat lower stroke is clear. Above it, two apparent stroke levels are merged into a dense rectangular patch, with several leftward starts; the patch prevents a secure count of original relation strokes.
The character after the relation has a tall slightly bent right stem and a distinct oblique arm descending left from its middle, forming lambda rather than a single numeral-1 stem.

Zero is a closed oval and t has a clear crossbar. The left comparator has an angular form with a thickened lower area, leaving < versus ≤ uncertain in this reading. Two strongly worked upright forms flank t; each has added curled or looped strokes. They may be cancelled vertical delimiters, but neither their identification as absolute-value bars nor their cancellation status is secure. The uncertainty wrappers cover each entire proposed cancelled delimiter.
The interlinear addition begins with a small separate a-shaped mark and a detached accent above it. A long down-and-up p is followed by connected low strokes with two separated i dots, giving priori.

The sequence has an initial loop and descending p stroke, a compressed connected ouvons group, then a separate low encore group, a short le, and a final définir group with an initial rise, a tall internal stroke and detached i dots. The four word groups remain visible despite the hurried horizontal joins.

The cancellation runs through nearly the whole two-character group. A taller first upright, a shorter second upright and a detached low dot remain, but the first letter curve and normal position of an i dot are obscured, so si cannot be established securely.

Under the sloping cancellation, a small initial oval is followed by a conspicuous tall l. Low curved remnants continue to the right, including the final rounded return below the cancellation; the visible outline supports alors.
The subscript beneath Delta has a long right stem with a diagonal lower-left branch, clearly making the two-legged lambda shape before +f.

Inside the parentheses the letter makes a tall left entry, a rounded bottom trough, and a right-hand rise followed by a short downstroke. That open trough and right stem support u; the terminal differential has a different rounded s-like return.
In the blue insertion after the opening parenthesis, a small rounded open o is followed by a low connected u with a right-hand rise and a short terminal stroke before the next zero.

The cancelled domain retains the loop and diagonal leg of R, a separate star below to its right, and a distinct raised plus with its own vertical stroke and horizontal crossbar. The plus is separate from the broad blue deletion strokes; the original candidate R_* omits it.

Across the horizontal cancellation, a right-facing opening bracket, closed oval 0, low comma, pointed double-stem M and left-facing terminal bracket remain visible. The terminal bracket is distinct from the blue enclosing underline.

After the equals sign the letter has a long descending left stroke, an ascending connection across its middle, and a separate right shoulder ending to the right. That descending stem and shoulder give mu rather than the simple v-shaped nu.

The letter before est has a retraced loop at the top of a long left descender and a right shoulder with a descending terminal. It is a heavily retraced mu; the descender and two-part upper body do not support nu.
After clockwise rotation, the heading has a tall looped capital L with its attached low e, then an upright b with a low loop, followed by the rounded low connection and final n-like rise of bon.

The line beneath Le bon contains separated short hook/dash groups and a raised stroke over the final low group, compatible with an accented où. The first groups are too compressed to distinguish the supplied cas from competing word divisions; three visible groups may include an extra short word.

Inside the crossed oval the faint word has an initial rounded loop rising into an ascender and a low undulating continuation. The diagonal cancellation intersects its middle; a dot and the alleged i/m boundaries cannot be separated securely from crossing strokes.

The first faint line begins with a small rounded mark and low trailing stroke for on, then shows a separate low hooked group before the tall descending p and terminal t of peut. The next line begins with a p-like descending stem and compressed r/end/re sequence for prendre. The extra hooked group may be ne, but its internal letters remain faint.

Following prendre, a small low hooked group and a separate taller double-stem group run toward the main-text bracket. The terminal stroke merges with that dark bracket/arrow; the faint forms do not securely identify a word or symbol.

The last oblique pencil line begins with a small accented a, then a tall l and detached apostrophe. The following low connected letters include dotted short stems and the taller f stroke, with a final dotted i, supporting à l’infini.
